title: University of Cambridge DE-GSJ Free Online Courses 2026: Apply for Fully Funded Sustainability, Climate and International Law Training
summary: Applications are open for the 2026 Fall Courses under the Democratising Education for Global Sustainability and Justice (DE-GSJ) Programme , an international educational initiative co-hosted by Lucy Cavendish College and Hughes Hall at the University of Cambridge . The programme provides learners around the world with free access to specialised education focused on sustainability, international law, public policy, climate change, biodiversity and sustainable development. For the 2026 Fall offering, applicants can express interest in courses addressing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), and the Paris Agreement . The Fall courses will run between September and November 2026, with the full application deadline set for 1 September 2026 at 11:59 PM BST . The DE-GSJ Programme is particularly valuable for law and policy leaders, government officials, academics, civil society professionals, practitioners and other individuals interested in using law and policy to address some of the world s most pressing sustainability and justice challenges. About the Democratising Education for Global Sustainability and Justice Programme The Democratising Education for Global Sustainability and Justice (DE-GSJ) Programme was created to harness the potential of international law to empower governments and communities around the world, with particular attention to highly vulnerable countries facing interconnected global crises. Co-hosted by Lucy Cavendish College and Hughes Hall at the University of Cambridge , the initiative makes education concerning the law and policy dimensions of sustainability more accessible to learners internationally. The programme also seeks to train law and policy specialists who can contribute to implementing essential international treaties at different levels of governance. Rather than approaching sustainability solely as an environmental issue, the programme explores the important relationship between sustainable development, international agreements, governance, public policy and legal frameworks. This gives participants an opportunity to understand not only major global sustainability challenges, but also how laws, treaties, institutions and policies can be used to translate international commitments into practical action. 2026 DE-GSJ Fall Courses The DE-GSJ educational offerings page states that applications are open for its Fall Courses 2026 . Three courses are included in the Fall 2026 schedule: Key Essentials: The Sustainable Development Goals and the Law Course dates: 28 September – 9 October 2026 Key Essentials: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), Sustainable Development and the Law Course dates: 12 October – 23 October 2026 Key Essentials: The Paris Agreement, Sustainable Development and the Law Course dates: 26 October – 6 November 2026 These dates allow learners to potentially build knowledge across several interconnected areas of international sustainability law during the Fall 2026 period. 1. Key Essentials: The Sustainable Development Goals and the Law The Key Essentials: The Sustainable Development Goals and the Law course provides an introduction to emerging approaches and frameworks in sustainable development law. It is designed for leaders and learners involved in areas such as: Law; Policymaking; Policy analysis; Legal and policy practice; Monitoring and reporting; Government; Academia; Civil society; and Practitioner communities. The course examines important challenges and possible solutions relating to sustainable development and considers the role that law can play in scaling up implementation globally and within learners own jurisdictions. Learning Objectives Through the course, learners are introduced to the relevance of sustainable development law and governance. Participants are encouraged to: Understand the relevance of sustainable development law and governance; Think critically about how sustainable development is reflected in legal and governance systems worldwide; Understand the role of governance within sustainable development law; Strengthen the role of law and policy in monitoring and reporting; and Explore opportunities to advance careers related to global sustainability and justice. Course Modules The Sustainable Development Goals and the Law course covers: Module 1: Introduction to the SDGs Module 2: Sustainable Development Law Principles and Practices Module 3: Law and Practice of SDGs in the Global Economy Module 4: Law and Practice of SDGs in the Global Biosphere Module 5: Law and Practice of SDGs Module 6: Course Conclusion and Final Remarks 2. Key Essentials: Convention on Biological Diversity, Sustainable Development and the Law The second Fall 2026 course focuses on biodiversity and the international legal frameworks designed to protect it. The programme highlights the seriousness of global biodiversity loss and provides learners with an overview of the Global Biodiversity Framework under the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity . It examines challenges, possible solutions and the role of law in strengthening implementation internationally and within individual jurisdictions. Learning Objectives Participants will have the opportunity to: Examine major biodiversity law and governance challenges; Explore the Global Biodiversity Framework; Understand tools available to policymakers and lawmakers, including those relating to finance, transparency and science; Identify and analyse innovative domestic legal and policy solutions; Strengthen understanding of monitoring and reporting through law and policy; and Develop knowledge relevant to careers in sustainability and justice. What Does the Biodiversity Course Cover? The course begins with an introduction to its structure and resources and includes engagement with instructors and learners from different parts of the world. Participants are introduced to the Convention on Biological Diversity , COP15 developments and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework . The subsequent modules explore several major areas. Nature Conservation, Ecosystem Restoration and Biodiversity Protection Learners examine international goals and targets related to reducing threats to biodiversity, slowing extinction, maintaining genetic diversity and expanding or improving natural ecosystems. Sustainable Use and Management of Biodiversity Participants explore international targets concerning sustainable biodiversity use and management, together with examples of regional, national and local policies. The course also examines international commitments concerning the sustainable use, harvesting and trade of wild species and their relationship with the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) . Benefit-Sharing and Traditional Indigenous Knowledge Learners explore international targets concerning access and benefit-sharing. The module introduces important international instruments including: The Nagoya Protocol; The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture; and The United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. It also considers the importance of protecting traditional knowledge. Biodiversity Finance and Capacity-Building Another module addresses the resources necessary to implement international biodiversity commitments, including: Financial resources; Capacity-building; Technical cooperation; Scientific cooperation; and Access to and transfer of technology. The course concludes with a live closing session and provides learners with insights into potential career paths related to the Global Biodiversity Framework, sustainable development and law. Learners are also invited to join a course alumni network. 3. Key Essentials: The Paris Agreement, Sustainable Development and the Law Climate change is another central focus of the Fall 2026 DE-GSJ programme. The Key Essentials: The Paris Agreement, Sustainable Development and the Law course introduces learners to the Paris Agreement under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) . The programme connects climate change with wider social, economic, environmental and human rights challenges and examines the role of law in responding to climate impacts and implementing international commitments. It is intended for leaders and learners working in law, policymaking, analysis, practice and reporting across governments, academia, civil society and practitioner communities. Learning Objectives The course seeks to help learners: Understand pressing climate change law and governance challenges; Explore the Paris Agreement; Understand tools available to policymakers and lawmakers, including climate finance, transparency and science; Identify innovative domestic policy and legal solutions; Strengthen the role of law and policy in monitoring and reporting; and Build knowledge relevant to international careers in sustainability and justice. What Will Participants Learn About the Paris Agreement? Course Introduction and Orientation Participants first become familiar with the course structure, resources, instructors and other learners. They are also introduced to the major elements, structures and principles of the Paris Agreement under the UNFCCC . Climate Mitigation and Net-Zero Transitions Learners examine mitigation obligations under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement, including legal commitments relating to the transition towards net zero. The module examines law and policy measures designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and efforts to limit average global warming. Climate Adaptation, Resilience and Loss and Damage Participants explore: Adaptation commitments under the Paris Agreement; Nationally Determined Contributions; National adaptation plans; Climate resilience; Legal and governance dimensions of adaptation; and Loss and Damage provisions and related international developments. Climate Finance and Carbon Markets Another module examines climate finance provisions under the Paris Agreement and international efforts to align financial flows with its goals. Learners are also introduced to carbon-market policy structures and low-greenhouse-gas development pathways. Climate Compliance, Capacity and Transparency Participants examine the Paris Agreement s enhanced transparency framework and the modalities, procedures and guidelines developed through subsequent Conferences of the Parties. The course also introduces the functions and objectives of the Paris Agreement Implementation and Compliance Committee (PAICC) . The final module includes a live closing session where instructors provide insights into climate law, governance and possible career pathways. Participants are also invited to join an alumni network. Course Format and Learning Experience The DE-GSJ courses are designed to combine expert instruction with flexible independent learning. According to the programme information provided, courses generally involve approximately eight to ten hours of total learning time , with focused modules delivered by University of Cambridge and international experts. The learning experience can include: Recorded or focused expert instruction; Live classroom engagements; Access to selected learning materials; Independent reading; Recommended resources; Self-paced study; Assessments; and Opportunities to engage with instructors and an international community of learners. For example, the programme describes one of its short courses as providing approximately eight hours of learning across six recorded modules, two live Zoom classroom engagements and approximately two to three hours of independent work. This structure makes the programme particularly relevant to professionals and learners who want intensive training without enrolling in a conventional full-time academic degree. Are the DE-GSJ Courses Free? Yes. The programme is designed to widen access to high-quality education, particularly for learners and professionals in countries that are highly vulnerable to climate and sustainability challenges. Successful applicants can undertake the course without paying the normal course value . Each selected learner effectively receives a bursary allowing them to complete the training at no charge. The programme information states that the course is valued at £800 . Importantly, this does not mean that successful participants receive £800 as a cash payment. Instead, the bursary covers access to the educational opportunity, meaning the selected learner does not have to pay the £800 course value. What Do Successful Learners Receive? The DE-GSJ initiative is a non-credit-bearing programme . This distinction is important for applicants who may otherwise assume that completing a course provides academic credits toward a University of Cambridge degree. However, successful completion offers other valuable professional-development benefits. Upon successfully completing each course, learners are eligible to receive a certificate from leading expert institutes of the University of Cambridge and global partners . Successful completion may also provide access to potential further scholarship opportunities for intensive professional development courses through Cambridge Advance Online . For professionals working in government, law, policy, international development, climate change, sustainability, human rights or civil society, the combination of specialised knowledge, certification and access to an international learning network can provide a useful foundation for continued professional development. Who Can Participate? The DE-GSJ Programme is primarily designed to train law and policy leaders . However, participation is not described as being exclusively restricted to lawyers or policymakers. Individuals who are committed to making a difference through law and policy in support of sustainable development may also seek to become part of the programme s wider community of practice. The individual courses specifically reference leaders and learners involved in: Government; Law; Policymaking; Policy analysis; Legal practice; Policy practice; Reporting and monitoring; Academia; Civil society; and Practitioner communities. This makes the opportunity potentially relevant to professionals and emerging leaders whose work intersects with sustainable development, environmental governance, climate action, biodiversity, international development or public policy. Is the Programme Available Internationally? Yes. The DE-GSJ Programme describes its mission in global terms and states that it provides free and accessible sustainability law and policy courses to learners from around the world , with particular emphasis on strengthening capacity in highly vulnerable countries. The supplied programme information does not state a restriction limiting the Fall 2026 courses to one nationality, race or continent. Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the application form and individual course requirements before applying. Language of Instruction The courses are currently offered only in English . Prospective participants should therefore consider whether they have sufficient English-language ability to follow expert instruction, complete readings and other independent learning activities, participate in live engagements and successfully complete required assessments. Certificates and Alumni Network Successful course completion can provide more than knowledge of a particular international agreement. Participants may become eligible for a certificate associated with leading University of Cambridge expert institutes and global partners. Individual courses also indicate that learners can be invited to become part of a course alumni network following completion. For example, both the biodiversity and Paris Agreement course descriptions reference invitations to join a network of course alumni. Such networks can help participants remain connected to a broader international community interested in sustainability, justice, international law and policy. How to Apply for the DE-GSJ Fall Courses 2026 The application process begins through the programme s Educational Offerings section. Applicants should follow these general steps: Review the available courses. Read the course descriptions and identify the Fall 2026 offering or offerings most relevant to your professional interests and development goals. Submit an Expression of Interest. Use the Expression of Interest form provided through the DE-GSJ Educational Offerings page. Check your email. After submitting the Expression of Interest form, prospective learners should receive further information and detailed instructions for completing the full application. Submit a separate application where required. Applicants interested in more than one course should follow the programme s instructions for submitting the necessary application for each course. Submit before the deadline. The programme states that applicants seeking consideration for the Fall Courses must submit their application by 1 September 2026 at 11:59 PM BST . Wait for the selection decision. Applications are reviewed by the programme s selection committee, and applicants are notified by email regarding whether they have been selected. Because participation is free for successful applicants, prospective learners should provide accurate and thoughtful information demonstrating their interest in the programme and their commitment to applying law and policy knowledge toward sustainable development. APPLY NOW Application Deadline The deadline for full applications to the DE-GSJ Fall Courses 2026 is: 1 September 2026 at 11:59 PM BST. Prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the deadline because the process begins with an Expression of Interest, after which additional application instructions are sent by email. Important Fall 2026 Dates Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Application deadline: 1 September 2026 at 11:59 PM BST Sustainable Development Goals and the Law: 28 September – 9 October 2026 Convention on Biological Diversity, Sustainable Development and the Law: 12 October – 23 October 2026 Paris Agreement, Sustainable Development and the Law: 26 October – 6 November 2026 Why Consider the DE-GSJ Programme? The programme provides an unusual opportunity to access specialised international sustainability law and policy education without paying the stated £800 course value. Potential advantages include: Free participation for successful applicants; Learning from University of Cambridge and global experts; Specialised training in sustainability law and governance; Flexible online and self-paced learning; Live classroom engagement; Exposure to an international community of learners; Training relating to major international treaties and frameworks; A certificate following successful completion; Access to an alumni network through relevant courses; Potential access to further scholarship opportunities for professional development through Cambridge Advance Online; and Knowledge that can potentially be applied in government, policy, law, academia, civil society and sustainability-related professional settings. The programme can be especially relevant for individuals seeking to connect global commitments such as the Sustainable Development Goals, Convention on Biological Diversity and Paris Agreement with practical legal and policy implementation. Conclusion The Democratising Education for Global Sustainability and Justice (DE-GSJ) Fall Courses 2026 provide an accessible pathway for professionals, emerging leaders and committed learners around the world to deepen their understanding of sustainability through the lens of international law and public policy. Co-hosted by Lucy Cavendish College and Hughes Hall at the University of Cambridge , the programme is particularly focused on building the capacity of law and policy specialists and empowering communities and governments, including those in highly vulnerable countries, to respond to interconnected global challenges. With Fall 2026 courses covering the Sustainable Development Goals, Convention on Biological Diversity and Paris Agreement , participants can engage with some of the most consequential international frameworks shaping sustainable development, biodiversity protection and global climate action. Successful applicants receive access to the training without paying the stated £800 course value, while successful completion can lead to certification, connections with an international alumni community and potential further professional-development scholarship opportunities. Interested candidates should review the available courses, submit their Expression of Interest and ensure that their full application is completed by 1 September 2026 at 11:59 PM BST . title: SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship: Fully Supported Fellowship for Early- to Mid-Career Professionals in Southeast Asia
summary: The SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship Programme offers an opportunity for early- to mid-career professionals working across human health, animal health, environmental health, climate change, and related One Health disciplines to gain practical experience with leading organizations and institutions across Southeast Asia. Organized by the Southeast Asia One Health University Network (SEAOHUN) , the fellowship is designed to strengthen the regional workforce’s capacity to understand and address climate-related health threats while promoting cross-sectoral collaboration, professional development, knowledge exchange, and evidence-based policy. The programme is particularly relevant for professionals who want to build expertise at the intersection of One Health and climate change and gain hands-on experience through a fellowship placement with a host organization. Opportunity category: Fellowship Application deadline: 20 September 2026 Fellowship period: Approximately four months, from November 2026 to February 2027 Location: Southeast Asia, at the assigned host organization What Is the SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship Programme? The SEAOHUN Fellowship Programme supports early- to mid-career professionals from SEAOHUN member countries by placing them with leading organizations and institutions where they can gain practical experience addressing One Health challenges. The 2026 programme has a particular focus on climate-related health challenges through the ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship . The fellowship recognizes that human health, animal health, environmental health, and climate change are interconnected. Climate change can affect disease transmission, ecosystems, food systems, biodiversity, water security, agriculture, and community health. Consequently, addressing emerging health threats increasingly requires professionals from different disciplines and countries to work together. The programme seeks to develop this capacity by connecting fellows with organizations across sectors, including: Academic institutions Research organizations Government agencies International organizations Non-governmental organizations Private-sector organizations Other institutions working on One Health and climate-related issues Through these placements, fellows can develop practical skills while working alongside national and international experts. Main Objectives of the ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship The fellowship is designed around several interconnected objectives. 1. Strengthen the One Health Workforce The programme seeks to develop a stronger workforce capable of responding to complex health challenges involving humans, animals, and the environment. 2. Address Climate-Related Health Threats Climate change is creating and intensifying a range of health challenges. The fellowship provides professionals with opportunities to develop practical knowledge and skills relevant to climate-health issues. 3. Promote Cross-Sectoral Collaboration One Health problems cannot always be addressed by a single profession or institution. The fellowship encourages collaboration across human health, veterinary medicine, environmental science, public health, biological sciences, climate science, and related fields. 4. Strengthen Cross-Country Cooperation The programme brings together professionals from different ASEAN countries and creates opportunities for regional knowledge exchange. 5. Generate Actionable Knowledge Fellows are expected to contribute to knowledge and outputs that can help inform climate-health policies and practices at both national and ASEAN levels. 6. Develop Professional Networks Working with established institutions and experts can help fellows develop professional relationships that continue beyond the fellowship period. Who Can Apply for the SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship? The programme is intended for early- to mid-career professionals with experience in One Health-related disciplines . Applicants should have an academic and/or professional background relevant to One Health and climate-related issues. title: Results for Development (R4D) Program Officer, Scaling Innovation Practice Job in Abuja, Nigeria 2026
summary: Results for Development (R4D) is hiring a Program Officer, Scaling Innovation Practice, in Abuja, Nigeria , offering an exciting opportunity for experienced professionals interested in global development, technology innovation, science and technology, innovation ecosystems, responsible artificial intelligence, and public policy. The full-time position will support R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice and contribute to the delivery of an upcoming programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO). The programme focuses on strengthening Nigeria’s science, technology and innovation (STI) ecosystem through partnerships, research-to-enterprise activities, and responsible artificial intelligence research. The position is based in Abuja, Nigeria , and operates under a hybrid working arrangement combining remote and in-office working days. It is a full-time role of 40 hours per week and is initially offered on a fixed-term basis through 31 March 2027 , with the possibility of an extension subject to funding. For professionals with experience in managing complex programmes, working with innovation ecosystems, engaging government and development partners, conducting research, and translating technical evidence into practical programmes, this R4D vacancy provides an opportunity to contribute directly to major innovation initiatives in Nigeria. About Results for Development Results for Development, commonly known as R4D, is a global nonprofit development organisation that works with change agents around the world to develop stronger systems capable of improving people s lives. R4D works alongside stakeholders including government officials, civil society leaders and social innovators. Its approach combines expertise in areas such as health, education and nutrition with analytical research, implementation support, practical decision-making and peer-learning networks. Rather than focusing solely on identifying development problems, R4D works with partners to determine how development objectives can be achieved and how effective systems can become sustainable over the long term. The organisation describes its workplace as collaborative, creative and entrepreneurial, with diversity, equity and inclusion playing an important role in both its organisational culture and mission. About R4D s Scaling Innovation Practice Innovation can play a major role in addressing complex global development challenges. Across areas including health, education, agriculture and finance, new approaches and technologies have contributed to significant improvements in people s lives. R4D s Scaling Innovation Practice works with partners to help identify, test, strengthen and scale promising solutions while supporting broader innovation systems. The practice engages a diverse range of actors at the global, regional and country levels. Its work includes helping partners overcome both supply-side and demand-side barriers that can prevent innovations from achieving greater impact. The team also works to strengthen innovation ecosystems by identifying and addressing gaps, weaknesses and inefficiencies that may prevent innovation from developing or scaling successfully. Stakeholders involved in this work can include: Social entrepreneurs National and subnational governments Civil society organisations Development agencies Researchers and research institutions Innovation ecosystem organisations Other development and technical partners R4D s Scaling Innovation Practice also contributes to international thought leadership through global innovation initiatives. These include the International Development Innovation Alliance (IDIA) , which connects innovation departments from leading development agencies, and the Million Lives Collective , a global multi-stakeholder network supporting proven innovations and their further scale-up. About the R4D Program Officer Opportunity in Nigeria R4D is recruiting a Program Officer to join its Scaling Innovation Practice in Abuja. The successful candidate will support the delivery of an upcoming UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office-funded science, technology and innovation programme in Nigeria . The programme requires full-time engagement at least until the end of March 2027 and is designed around three complementary workstreams intended to strengthen Nigeria s science, technology and innovation ecosystem. 1. UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership The first workstream focuses on a UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership. The Program Officer will contribute to activities such as researching priority sectors, examining international good practices for science and technology cluster models, supporting ecosystem diagnostics, and assessing opportunities that could generate mutual benefits for Nigeria and the United Kingdom. 2. Research-to-Enterprise Pilot The second workstream is a Research-to-Enterprise Pilot involving selected research institutions. This area of work will explore approaches for connecting research more effectively with enterprise, including research commercialisation and knowledge transfer. The Program Officer will contribute research, analysis and technical input to help understand which international models and practices could be relevant to the Nigerian context. 3. Responsible AI Research Initiative The third workstream focuses on responsible artificial intelligence research. The initiative will connect Nigerian and UK-based researchers around priorities associated with Nigeria s national AI agenda. The successful candidate may therefore contribute to research and stakeholder engagement involving responsible AI governance and related innovation policy issues. Together, the three workstreams place the successful applicant at the intersection of science, technology, innovation, research commercialisation, entrepreneurship and responsible AI . What the Program Officer Will Do The Program Officer will take responsibility for significant elements of the Nigeria programme while working as an integral member of R4D s broader Innovation team. R4D operates a matrixed resourcing structure, meaning team members may contribute their expertise across different programmes and projects. As a result, the successful candidate may also have opportunities to contribute technical knowledge relating to innovation scaling, innovation ecosystems, innovation policy and practice to other programmes within R4D s portfolio. The organisation is specifically looking for someone who is entrepreneurial, strategic and highly organised. Candidates should be comfortable managing multiple projects and working with geographically dispersed teams, funders, contracts and partnerships while maintaining strong standards for risk management and deliverable quality. Experience in technology innovation, innovation ecosystem strengthening, responsible AI, or science and technology policy is required for the position. Key Responsibilities The responsibilities of the R4D Program Officer are divided into four major areas. 1. Project and Programme Management The successful candidate will support and lead important elements of programme delivery. Responsibilities include: Leading significant components of the UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership and Research-to-Enterprise Pilot. Researching priority sectors. Reviewing international good practices relating to cluster models and research-to-enterprise approaches. Supporting the innovation ecosystem diagnostic process. Developing and implementing individual workplans aligned with wider programme timelines. Ensuring innovation activities are delivered on time and to a high standard. Producing high-quality programme deliverables with appropriate senior guidance. Supporting data collection for the programme s monitoring, evaluation and learning strategy. Collecting relevant stakeholder and innovation ecosystem information. Identifying and proactively managing risks and programme issues. Proposing practical options for resolving challenges. Contributing to and taking ownership of funder progress reports and updates. Supporting procurement, budgeting and resourcing processes. Contributing to internal evaluations of programme and project progress. Technical Research and Analysis Responsibilities The Program Officer will also provide substantive technical and analytical input across the programme s three workstreams. This will include conducting rapid research and stakeholder mapping relating to priority sectors being considered for the UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster. The successful applicant will be expected to produce evidence-based briefs explaining potential sector opportunities and the possible mutual benefits for Nigeria and the United Kingdom. Other technical responsibilities include: Reviewing draft innovation ecosystem diagnostics. Providing substantive input based on international good practices and lessons relating to cluster models. Examining research-to-enterprise approaches. Reviewing international evidence concerning research commercialisation. Exploring knowledge-transfer approaches. Reviewing responsible AI governance models that may be relevant to Nigeria. Developing technical and analytical reports, tools and frameworks. Contributing new knowledge and approaches relating to innovation ecosystems. Supporting work relating to research commercialisation and responsible AI. The successful candidate may lead the development of technical and analytical products across the programme s three workstreams, with some senior-level support. Partner and Stakeholder Engagement Relationship management will be another major component of the position. The Program Officer will establish and maintain collaborative relationships with partners and stakeholders throughout the innovation ecosystem. These may include: Government ministries Government agencies Research institutions Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises Innovation ecosystem organisations Downstream delivery partners Researchers Private-sector stakeholders Other programme partners The Program Officer will need to communicate technical information clearly and develop impactful content suitable for audiences such as government officials, research institutions and private-sector stakeholders. The role will also involve supporting and, in some instances, leading stakeholder workshops and convenings across the programme s three workstreams. Responsibilities can extend to workshop logistics, facilitation and documentation. Another important element will be supporting engagement with the UK-based Nigerian research diaspora community as part of the responsible AI research initiative. Contributing to R4D s Wider Innovation Strategy The successful candidate will not be limited exclusively to day-to-day programme implementation. They will also contribute to strengthening R4D s Scaling Innovation Practice. Potential responsibilities include: Producing thought-leadership materials. Developing or improving methods and tools used by the Innovation Practice. Supporting operational improvement initiatives. Contributing to recruitment activities when required. Supporting business development. Contributing to funding proposals. Writing sections of proposals. Representing R4D and the Innovation Practice at meetings. Participating in conferences and relevant events. Contributing to R4D s internal networks. Supporting organisational improvement initiatives. Qualifications and Experience Required Applicants must meet substantial academic and professional experience requirements. R4D states that candidates should have either: A Master s degree plus at least three years of relevant experience ; or A Bachelor s degree plus at least five years of relevant experience . Ideally, the qualification should be in a relevant discipline such as: Global development Public policy Science and technology Innovation Another relevant field However, R4D indicates that candidates with other qualifications providing an equivalent level of professional experience may also be considered. Essential Professional Experience Beyond academic qualifications, applicants need relevant programme and technical experience. Essential requirements include experience in programme and project management within areas such as: Global development Innovation Science and technology Related ecosystem-based programmes Candidates must also have experience working in technology innovation, scaling innovation and/or strengthening innovation ecosystems. Applicants should demonstrate excellent writing, communication and presentation capabilities. This includes experience producing high-quality outputs and facilitating engagement with senior-level or multi-stakeholder audiences, both virtually and in person. R4D is also seeking candidates who have experience working effectively in matrixed environments involving multiple programmes, teams or workstreams. Relationship Management and Donor-Funded Programme Experience Candidates should be able to demonstrate experience developing and managing relationships with diverse development stakeholders at both country and global levels. These stakeholders may include: Government actors Think tanks Innovation ecosystem organisations Technical partners Development partners Experience managing components of donor-funded programmes is also essential. R4D specifically mentions FCDO-funded programmes or equivalent experience, including coordinating with partners, subcontractors or implementing organisations. Skills and Personal Qualities R4D Is Looking For The organisation is seeking candidates who understand innovation and scaling processes as well as innovation ecosystems. Applicants should demonstrate that they are: Strategic and creative problem-solvers. Highly collaborative and approachable. Comfortable working closely with colleagues. Highly organised. Detail-oriented. Professional and reliable. Able to prioritise competing responsibilities. Capable of working across multiple projects and workstreams. Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment. Able to exercise good judgement. Capable of working independently. Effective contributors within teams. Willing to operate in environments that may sometimes involve ambiguity. Candidates must also be willing to travel occasionally according to project needs. R4D estimates that travel could amount to a maximum of approximately three to four weeks per year . Legal Right to Work in Nigeria An especially important eligibility requirement is that all applicants must already be legally authorised to work in Nigeria . Prospective applicants should carefully consider this condition before applying, particularly those applying from outside Nigeria. The vacancy information does not indicate that visa sponsorship or relocation assistance will be provided. Candidates should therefore not assume that sponsorship is available unless R4D confirms this separately. Highly Desirable Qualifications and Experience In addition to the essential criteria, R4D identifies several qualifications and areas of experience that would strengthen an application. These include: A professional qualification in project or programme management. Experience using innovation methodologies. Experience with user-centred design. Experience with agile methodologies. Experience with adaptive learning. Experience working directly with innovators or entrepreneurs. Experience working with other actors within innovation ecosystems. These criteria are described as highly desirable rather than essential, meaning candidates should distinguish them from the mandatory requirements when assessing their suitability. Salary for the R4D Program Officer Position The vacancy lists a potential salary of NGN 13,330,000 , with actual compensation dependent on experience and other compensable factors. R4D states that it seeks to provide equitable and consistent starting salaries for new hires based on the responsibilities and qualifications associated with each position. The organisation also notes that the broader salary range is intended to provide opportunities for future career and earnings growth. R4D Employee Benefits Base salary represents only one component of R4D s total rewards package. According to the vacancy announcement, R4D s benefits package includes: Medical insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance Open personal leave 15 days of paid sick leave Paid holidays Paid parental leave Pension contributions Company-paid life insurance Short-term disability insurance Long-term disability insurance Employee assistance programme Flexible working environment R4D notes that international hiring ranges and benefit packages can differ depending on location. Applicants should therefore confirm which benefits apply specifically to the Nigeria-based position during the recruitment process. Please visit our R4D Careers page for more details Work Location and Employment Arrangement The Program Officer position is based in Abuja, Nigeria . Why This Opportunity Could Be Particularly Relevant for Innovation Professionals The R4D Program Officer opportunity brings together several rapidly developing areas of international development.
